newsitem.title: USA: US spot gas mostly steady ahead of cooler weather.
newsitem.headline: US spot gas mostly steady ahead of cooler weather.

text.p: U.S. spot natural gas prices were little changed Thursday as cooler temperatures were expected to arrive in the Midwest and East this weekend, industry sources said.
Keeping the lid on prices, however, are the six- to 10-day forecasts calling for normal to above-normal temperatures across the U.S.
Louisiana Gulf Coast prices were down an average of two cents to the high-$1.80s, with Henry Hub quoted mostly in the low-$1.90s.
As March bidweek nears, traders are reporting closing swing swap deals below index levels.
Traders blame the softness on ample storage supplies and the anticipated normal drop in demand in March.

American Gas Association reported Wednesday that U.S. gas inventories as of Feb 14 were down 147 bcf to 35 percent of capacity. In the East, stocks at 687 bcf were 233 bcf, or 51 percent above year-ago.
In south Texas, prices slid nine cents to the $1.70-1.75 range.
Permian gas prices were up one cent to the $1.65-1.70 area, while southern California border prices were also slightly higher in the low-to-mid $1.70s.
Southern California Edison said earlier today that the restart of its 1,070 megawatt San Onofre 2 nuclear power unit would likely be delayed until early March.
In the Midcontinent, prices slipped two cents to the low-$1.70s, with Demarcation quoted mostly around $1.75.
Chicago city-gate values were talked in the low-$1.90s.
In the East, New York city-gate prices were constant in the $2.15-2.20 range.
